title: Replace a cut-out drain-pipe section with slip couplings
instruction: Fit the orange section into the gap in the grey drain pipe and join both ends with the black slip couplings that fit.
context: Replace a cracked length of drain pipe: dry-fit a new section into the cut-out gap with two slip couplings. A closed coupling cannot get onto a run captured at both ends, so both go onto the old pipe ends (or the new piece) before the gap closes, then slide back over the joints. Only one size among look-alikes fits. A steel support with PTFE slide liners holds the new section while each arm slides its own coupling. Plumbers (O*NET 47-2152.00: "Assemble pipe sections, tubing, or fittings, using couplings, clamps, screws, bolts, cement, plastic solvent ...") and general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00) do this dry fit before cement.
setup: Positions are in mm, forward of the line through the two arm bases and left or right (robot's view) of the point midway between them; heights are above the 747.5 mm table top. The arm bases are 305 mm left and right of that point. Old drain run, fixed to the bench: grey PVC-U pipe, 32 mm outside diameter, running left-right 200 mm forward with its axis 70 mm above the table. A 344 mm length has been cut out, leaving two stubs that run from 172 to 300 mm left and right of centre; each cut end has a 2 mm long, 28 mm diameter chamfer step. At 307 mm left and right a grey PVC-U elbow, 38 mm outside diameter, turns each stub down into a 32 mm diameter vertical riser standing on the table. A galvanised-steel pipe clamp holds each stub at 279 mm left and right: a post 12 mm forward-back, 8 mm left-right and 54 mm tall under the pipe, its centre 43 mm below the axis, and a strap 8 mm wide along the pipe, made of a 44 by 4 mm top bar centred 18 mm above the axis and two 4 by 32 mm side bars centred 20 mm in front of and behind the axis. Replacement section, loose: orange PVC-U drain pipe, 330 mm long, 32 mm outside diameter, 1.5 mm wall, 63 g, with a 1.9 mm long, 28 mm diameter chamfer step on each cut end. It lies left-right, centred 280 mm forward and 20 mm right, axis 31 mm above the table (bottom 15 mm), on two fixed grey PVC-U rails, each 5 mm wide, 126 mm long and 15.1 mm tall, centred 273 and 287 mm forward and 20 mm right; their inner top edges touch the pipe 4.5 mm either side of its lowest line. Pipe support, fixed, under the gap: a grey steel stand with PTFE slide liners, 109.2 mm forward-back by 140 mm left-right, centred 200 mm forward on the midline. Its two shoulders are 54.1 mm tall either side of a 9 mm wide centre channel; their inner edges touch the pipe 4.5 mm either side of its lowest line and hold its axis 69.5 mm above the table, 0.5 mm below the run. Two round guide bars, 38 mm diameter and 140 mm long, run left-right along its front and back edges at 164.4 and 235.6 mm forward, axes 69.5 mm high, leaving 0.6 mm side clearance to the pipe. Couplings, loose, black ABS, each lying forward-back with its centre 120 mm forward and its bottom 8.5 mm above the table: two matching slip couplings (repair couplings with no centre stop), 80 mm long, 34 mm bore, 52 mm outside diameter, 30 g, centred 260 mm left and 260 mm right; a small look-alike, 60 mm long, 23 mm bore, 40 mm outside diameter, 15 g, 380 mm left; a large look-alike, 80 mm long, 43.5 mm bore, 65 mm outside diameter, 40 g, 367 mm right. The matching couplings have rounded mouths, the look-alikes square-cut ones. Trays, fixed: two grey polypropylene trays with rubber-lined floors, centred 120 mm forward and 320 mm left and right; each floor is 90 mm forward-back by 230 mm left-right by 4 mm thick, with 4 mm wide, 8 mm tall rims along its front and back edges and open left and right ends. Each coupling rests on four grey rubber blocks, 6 by 4 mm in plan and 8.5 mm tall (8.4 mm under the large look-alike), 30 mm either side of its centre along its length and 4 mm either side of its axis. Friction, static/dynamic: PVC-U and ABS 0.6/0.5, rubber 1.2/1.0, PTFE 0.05/0.04.
scoring: End-state tiers; either matching coupling may join either end. In line: section axis within 4 degrees of the pipe line (200 mm forward, 70 mm above the table); both end centres within 5 mm radially of that line; both ends between the cut faces, 172 mm left and right of centre, allowing 2 mm axial penetration. Coupled: a matching coupling's axis within 5 degrees of the pipe line, its centre within 3 mm radially, overlapping both the stub and the section by at least 25 mm along the pipe. On run: the same 5-degree/3 mm alignment and at least 25 mm overlap with a stub, or with the section on the section's own axis, including while the section is on its start rails. 1.0: section in line, both joints coupled, and the section and both matching couplings released and still, continuously for 1 s. Released: each gripper's centre point between the pads at least 3 cm from each of these three parts' bounding boxes. Still: over the last 1.0 s, each part's centre stays within 1.0 mm of where it ends and its axis direction within 1.0 degree of its final direction; spin about a part's own axis does not count, as a round pipe or coupling can turn without moving the assembly. Alignment, coupling and release must hold over that same second. Below 1.0, release and stillness are not required. 0.75: section in line and both joints coupled, but held, moving or short of the 1 s hold. 0.5: section in line and either exactly one joint coupled (the other coupling anywhere) or both matching couplings on run. 0.25: both matching couplings on run, including parked on stubs or section, section not in line. 0: every other outcome, including the untouched start and the section in line with no joint coupled and not both couplings on run. Parts may be set down on the bench. Permanent 0 for the episode if any point of the section or a matching sleeve ever goes more than 10 mm below the bench top (bench top 0.7475 m, so below 0.7375 m), i.e. off the bench; picking it back up does not clear it. Look-alikes are not checked and never count: the small one cannot fit the 32 mm pipe; the large one hangs at least 5.75 mm off-axis, beyond 3 mm. Success requires score 1.0 for a further 1 s. A real trial is measured with a tape along the pipe for each coupling's overlap on its stub and on the section, a straight edge across both stubs for the section being in line, and the video for stillness and the 3 cm hand clearance.
reset_notes: Return all five free parts to their listed cradle poses. Reset episode history and timers. The pipe support stays fixed. Fixed layout, object_jitter=0; seeds do not change it. No consumables; no cement.
fidelity: Rigid primitives with 1 mm contact offsets. Pipes have solid interiors; the section's end portions are faceted within 1.9 mm of round. Coupling walls are overlapping rods (ball-capped on matching ones, square-cut on look-alikes) with diagonal bore relief and an inner wall web; the 1 mm radial clearance is looser than a gasketed coupling. A fixed PTFE-lined steel V-seat and guides align the span. No cement, seal, fluid or deformation; run and clamps fixed.
